newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to allow warrant issues in June - minister.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to allow warrant issues in June - minister.

text.p: Taiwan's Finance Minister Paul Chiu said on Saturday the island is expected to allow local and foreign institutions to issue warrants on Taiwan stocks by the end of June.
"The rule governing warrants issuance is expected to have cabinet approval by the end of April and is expected to take into effect by the end of June," Chiu told reporters.
Local and foreign banks or securities brokerages need to have capital of T$3 billion to issue warrants on local listed firms, Chiu said.
Warrants would be traded at the Taiwan Stock Exchange, the minister said.

Under the proposed rule, local and foreign institutions would be allowed to issue warrants on domestic blue chips having a market value of more than T$30 billion and 25 percent or more of their shares circulating in the market.
To be eligible, listed companies also must have more than 7,500 shareholders, officials have said.
More than 20 local listed companies, including Cathay Life, Chang Hwa Bank, First Bank, Hua Nan Bank, Nan Ya Plastics, Formosa Plastics and China Steel, gualify under the proposed guidelines.
